chunks: Yaḥyā ibn al-Qushayrī from a village called Qīr narrated to me; he said:

Abū Muḥammad had an agent who had taken for himself a room in the house, and with him there was a white servant. The agent desired the servant for himself, but he refused unless he brought him nabīdh. So he contrived to get nabīdh for him, then brought it in to him, while between him and Abū Muḥammad there were three locked doors.

He said: The agent narrated to me, saying: I was alert when suddenly the doors were opening until he himself came and stood at the door of the room. Then he said: O you people, have taqwa of Allah; fear Allah. So when morning came, he ordered that the servant be sold and that I be removed from the house.

key_terms.أَبْوَابٍ مُغْلَقَةٍ: locked doors, emphasizing physical separation and concealment
key_terms.اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: have taqwa of Allah; a command to act with God-consciousness
key_terms.خَادِمٌ: a servant attending within the household
key_terms.خَافُوا اللَّهَ: fear Allah; an admonition against sinful conduct
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ: nabidh, a fermented drink mentioned here as something sought before the act
key_terms.وَكِيلٌ: an appointed agent or representative serving on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the moral authority and awareness of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident involving the agent of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, whose misconduct with a servant was exposed despite multiple locked doors separating them from the Imam عليه السلام. The narration highlights the Imam’s awareness, his moral admonition, and his decisive response to wrongdoing.
